theme_report <- function(base_size = 11.5) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1),
      axis.title       = element_text(size = base_size - 0.5),
      axis.text        = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5, color = "grey20"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5),
      legend.text      = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5),
      plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_report())

tagged <- function(p) {
  p + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_suffix = ".") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
}

show_tbl <- function(x, caption = NULL, ...) {
  kbl(x, caption = caption, booktabs = TRUE, ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
}

```{python init-paths, include=FALSE}
import json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

RES_ROOT = Path(r.RES_DIR)

def res_path(*parts):
    cand = RES_ROOT.joinpath(*parts)
    if cand.exists():
        return cand
    if parts and parts[0] == "falsification_controls":
        fb = RES_ROOT.joinpath("exp6_referee_falsifications", *parts[1:])
        if fb.exists():
            return fb
    if (RES_ROOT / "salvage").exists():
        cand2 = RES_ROOT.joinpath("salvage", *parts)
        if cand2.exists():
            return cand2
        if parts and parts[0] == "falsification_controls":
            fb2 = RES_ROOT.joinpath("salvage", "exp6_referee_falsifications", *parts[1:])
            if fb2.exists():
                return fb2
    return cand

def load_fc_summary():
    raw = json.loads(res_path("falsification_controls", "summary.json").read_text())
    if "disattenuation" in raw:
        return raw
    return {
        "disattenuation": raw["exp6a_disattenuation"],
        "monte_controls": raw["exp6b_monte_controls"],
        "newey_external": raw["exp6c_newey_external"],
        "hap1_2x2_sec61": raw["exp6d_hap1_2x2_sec61"],
        "persistence_controls": raw["exp6e_persistence_controls"],
    }
```

# Cross-Lineage Perturbation Transfer (`35` Contrasts, `16` Lineages) and `I=L` Sensitivity

### Rationale

With single-biopsy profiles bounded near chance by inherited HLA polymorphism and stromal confounding, I next test whether paired compositional shifts $\Delta q_s = \Phi(\pi_{s,1} - \pi_{s,0})$ classify IFN-$\gamma$ versus MAPK inhibition across `35` longitudinal perturbation contrasts spanning `16` human lineages and five independent studies. To prevent information leakage, nested regularization penalties are selected strictly inside outer training splits leaving out entire cell lineages (LOLO) or entire studies (LOSO). I also test mass-spectrometric isoleucine/leucine harmonization (`I=L`) because `Bernhardt Table 4` reports `I/L` ambiguities differently from `Tables 7–11`.

```{python cross-lineage-tables}
cross_t = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp7_distributional_sensing", "exp7c_cross_lineage_study_transfer.tsv"), sep="\t")
il_t    = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp7_distributional_sensing", "exp7c_isobaric_il_sensitivity.tsv"), sep="\t")
loc_t   = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp7_distributional_sensing", "exp7c_within_vs_between_locus_decomposition.tsv"), sep="\t")
st_sup  = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "study_class_support_and_within_study_metrics.csv"))
ko_dec  = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "kitagawa_oaxaca_locus_vs_motif_decomposition.csv"))
ext_br  = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "external_frozen_decoder_bridge_results.csv"))
ext_pr  = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "external_aranha2026_pxd085506_proteome_state.csv"))
```

```{r fig-cross-lineage-loc, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.4}
p_cl <- py$cross_t |>
  mutate(Rep = factor(representation, levels = rev(representation))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(lolo_auroc, loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc), names_to = "Regime", values_to = "AUROC") |>
  mutate(Regime = recode(Regime, lolo_auroc = "LOLO (16 lineages)", loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc = "Strict LOSO (5 studies)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Rep, y = AUROC, fill = Regime)) +

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = GRAY) +

  ylim(0, 1.02) +

p_loc <- py$loc_t |>
  mutate(Comp = factor(decomposition_component, levels = rev(decomposition_component)),
         IsBetween = grepl("Between", decomposition_component)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Comp, y = lolo_auroc, fill = IsBetween)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.58) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = GRAY) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = TEAL, "FALSE" = NAVY), guide = "none") +

  labs(x = NULL, y = "LOLO AUROC (20 contrasts)", title = "Locus reallocation vs. within-locus motifs")

tagged(p_cl + p_loc)
```

**What do we see?**

Tables 3.1–3.3 and Figure 3.1 establish both cross-lineage transfer performance and its biophysical mechanism:

- **Full `PosAA180` beats anchor-blind `Coarse96` under strict transfer:** Across `35` paired contrasts (`16` human lineages), `PosAA180` achieves `LOLO AUROC = 0.948` (`86%` balanced accuracy) and strict disjoint-study `LOSO AUROC = 0.756` (`68%` balanced accuracy), whereas anchor-blind `Coarse96` drops to `0.724` in `LOLO` and fails at **`0.448`** in strict `LOSO`. P2+P9 anchor marginals alone (`Anchor40`) reach `0.936` in `LOLO` (`0.588` in `LOSO`), confirming that P2/P9 HLA pocket shifts drive cross-lineage decoding.
- **Isobaric `I=L` harmonization lifts strict cross-study transfer above source-gene shares:** Because `Bernhardt Table 4` (MaxQuant) distinguishes database `I` vs. `L` whereas `Tables 7–11` (Peptide-PRISM) collapse `I -> L`, canonical MS-isobaric `I=L` harmonization eliminates cross-table coding mismatch and raises strict study+lineage-purged `PosAA180 LOSO AUROC` from `0.756` to **`0.788`** (`LOLO = 0.916`, Table 3.2), exceeding `SourceGene_Oracle` (`0.776`) and `Anchor40` (`0.560`).
- **Exact symmetric Kitagawa–Oaxaca decomposition (`35` donor-genotyped contrasts, Table 3.3):** Projecting the exact algebraic identity $\Delta q = \sum_\ell \Delta w_\ell \bar{\mu}_\ell + \sum_\ell \bar{w}_\ell \Delta\mu_\ell$ (`max residual < 1e-16`, retaining unassigned mass explicitly) onto the frozen outer-fold `PosAA180 (I=L)` decoder shows equal `LOLO` contributions (`51.8%` between-locus / `48.2%` within-locus), whereas under strict cross-study `LOSO`, **`76.8%` (`75.3%` under soft multi-locus assignment) of the frozen linear class gap arises from within-locus motif remodeling** (`AUROC = 0.796` vs. `0.780` between-locus). In parallel standalone refits, assigned coverage alone (`1 df`) has no signal (`LOSO = 0.168`), whereas conditional `HLA-A/B/C` reallocation given assigned (`2 df`) reaches `LOLO = 0.936` and `LOSO = 0.924` (`0.879` / `0.808` on the 20-contrast author subset).

# Zero-HLA-Overlap Drug Resistance (`SK-Mel-28 wt vs. dr`) and Cross-Platform Transfer

### Rationale

To prove that paired 9-mer shifts decode signaling state rather than shared HLA binding motifs or drug presence alone, I evaluate an extreme out-of-genotype challenge in `Bernhardt 2025`: train strictly on `Ma-Mel-63a` and `UKE-Mel-105b` (`7` total 4-digit alleles) and score all eight `SK-Mel-28` runs (sensitive `wt` vs. double-resistant `dr` under identical vemurafenib + cobimetinib exposure vs. Mock DMSO at 24 h and 72 h), where `SK-Mel-28` shares **zero** 4-digit HLA alleles with training. I also evaluate cross-platform transfer from `Stopfer 2022` `TMT` positives plus `pSILAC` Mock controls to unseen `Bernhardt pSILAC` runs.

```{python skmel28-challenge}
res_t = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp7_distributional_sensing", "exp7c_resistance_and_cross_study_challenge.tsv"), sep="\t")
sk_t  = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "skmel28_predictions_with_il_and_unseen_9mer_purge.csv"))
did_t = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp8_immunity_bridge", "skmel28_mock_adjusted_did.csv"))
sk_view = sk_t[["contrast_id", "cell_subline", "time_h", "is_drug_exposed", "d_mda_share_pct", "score_R1_Coarse96", "score_R2_PosAA180", "score_R2_PosAA180_IL", "score_R2_PosAA180_IL_Unseen9mersOnly"]]
```

```{r fig-skmel28-transfer, fig.width=9.8, fig.height=4.4}
skp <- py$sk_t |>
  mutate(Group = factor(case_when(
    cell_subline == "SKMel28_wt" & is_drug_exposed == 1 ~ "wt + Vemu/Cobi\n(Sensitive)",
    cell_subline == "SKMel28_dr" & is_drug_exposed == 1 ~ "dr + Vemu/Cobi\n(Resistant)",
    cell_subline == "SKMel28_wt" & is_drug_exposed == 0 ~ "wt + Mock\n(DMSO)",
    TRUE ~ "dr + Mock\n(DMSO)"
  ), levels = c("wt + Mock\n(DMSO)", "dr + Mock\n(DMSO)", "dr + Vemu/Cobi\n(Resistant)", "wt + Vemu/Cobi\n(Sensitive)")))

p_sk1 <- ggplot(skp, aes(x = Group, y = score_R2_PosAA180, color = Group, shape = factor(time_h))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(size = 3.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.25)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("wt + Vemu/Cobi\n(Sensitive)" = TEAL, "dr + Vemu/Cobi\n(Resistant)" = ORANGE, "wt + Mock\n(DMSO)" = LBLUE, "dr + Mock\n(DMSO)" = GRAY)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Out-of-lineage PosAA180 score", shape = "Time (h)", title = "PosAA180 transfer (0 shared 4-digit HLAs)")

p_sk2 <- ggplot(skp, aes(x = Group, y = d_mda_share_pct, color = Group, shape = factor(time_h))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(size = 3.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.25)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("wt + Vemu/Cobi\n(Sensitive)" = TEAL, "dr + Vemu/Cobi\n(Resistant)" = ORANGE, "wt + Mock\n(DMSO)" = LBLUE, "dr + Mock\n(DMSO)" = GRAY)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Melanoma diff. antigen (MDA) delta share (%)", shape = "Time (h)", title = "8-gene MDA share transfer across platforms")

tagged(p_sk1 + p_sk2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")) & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**What do we see?**

Tables 3.4–3.5 and Figure 3.2 demonstrate out-of-genotype biological state decoding under complete four-digit HLA disjointness:

- **Zero-HLA-overlap `SK-Mel-28 wt vs. dr` (`exact p = 0.0357`):** Trained strictly on `Ma-Mel-63a + UKE-Mel-105b` (`n = 14`), `PosAA180` scores both sensitive `wt + VemuCobi` runs sharply positive (`+8.676` at 24 h, `+9.624` at 72 h, mean `+9.150`), whereas double-resistant `dr + VemuCobi` under identical drug treatment sits at `-3.332` (24 h) and `+0.912` (72 h, mean `-1.210`, mean gap `+10.360`) and all four DMSO controls stay negative (`-8.568` to `-5.747`). This yields **`AUROC = 1.000`** (`concordance = 1.00`, combinatorial `p = 1/28 = 0.0357`), identical to the prespecified 8-gene melanoma differentiation antigen axis (`R5b`, `+1.870%` / `+4.832%` in `wt` vs. `+0.318%` / `+0.860%` in `dr`).
- **Disqualified drug-exposure shortcut and anchor-blind `Coarse96`:** A model matching drug presence alone outputs `+5.527` symmetrically for both `wt` and `dr` treated runs (`treated concordance = 0.500`, `p = 0.1786`), while `Coarse96` collapses to `AUROC = 0.250` (`concordance = 0.500`).
- **Cross-platform `TMT -> pSILAC` boundary:** Whole-repertoire `PosAA180` trained on `Stopfer 2022` `TMT` drops to `0.667` on `SK-Mel-28` (`0.417` across all 14 unseen Bernhardt runs) due to quantitation chemistry shifts, whereas normalized `R5b` gene-share transfers directly across platforms (`1.000` on `SK-Mel-28`, `0.917` across all 14 unseen `pSILAC` runs).

# Six-Omic Tumor Degradative Flux and Endogenous ERAP1 Trimming (`Abelin MONTE` LUAD)

### Rationale

To establish the in vivo biochemical channels feeding HLA-I surface dynamics inside human tumors, I examine all six paired molecular layers across `N=10` primary lung adenocarcinomas (`Abelin MONTE`): (1) across-gene regressions (`N=7,594` proteins) comparing `HLA-I` vs. `HLA-II` peptide breadth against `K-epsilon-GG` ubiquitylation, phosphorylation, acetylation, and `UniProt` secretory/ER/membrane topology—both before and after adjusting for $\log_2(1 + N_{\mathrm{Lys}})$ lysine residue density; (2) within-gene across-patient regressions comparing independent non-depleted `noIP` vs. serial flow-through `FT` tissue aliquots alongside exact Gauss-Seidel two-way demeaning with Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2011) two-way clustered standard errors and `2SLS` instrumental-variable (`FT -> noIP`) checks; and (3) patient-level correlations linking tumor `APPM` core proteome to `HLA-I` repertoire breadth (with tumor purity and `ESTIMATE` immune controls + 10-tumor jackknife) and `ERAP1` protein levels to peptide length within all `16` shared four-digit HLA-I alleles.

```{python monte-six-omic}

m2_flux = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp2_monte_degradative_flux", "within_gene_across_patient_flux.tsv"), sep="\t")

m2_pt   = pd.read_csv(res_path("exp2_monte_degradative_flux", "monte_patient_appm_and_ligandome.tsv"), sep="\t")
m_lys   = pd.read_csv(res_path("falsification_controls", "monte_lysine_controlled_regression.tsv"), sep="\t")
m_al    = pd.read_csv(res_path("falsification_controls", "monte_within_exact_allele_erap1.tsv"), sep="\t")

m2_ctrl_tbl = pd.DataFrame([
    {"Check": "Lysine-adjusted K-eps-GG HLA-I beta", "Estimate": round(mc["lysine_controlled_hlai_ub_beta"], 4), "Detail": f"p = {mc['lysine_controlled_hlai_ub_p']:.2e}; diff (I-II) beta = {mc['lysine_controlled_diff_ub_beta']:.4f} (p={mc['lysine_controlled_diff_ub_p']:.4f})"},
    {"Check": "Gauss-Seidel 2-way FE within-gene Ub (noIP, N=9,910)", "Estimate": round(mc["exact_2way_noip_beta_ub"], 4), "Detail": f"2-way CGM SE = {mc['exact_2way_noip_se2way_ub']:.4f}; Prot beta = {mc['exact_2way_noip_beta_prot']:.4f}"},
    {"Check": "2SLS IV (FT instrumenting noIP)", "Estimate": round(mc["iv_2sls_beta_prot"], 4), "Detail": f"Ub IV beta = {mc['iv_2sls_beta_ub']:.4f}; FT-noIP residual r = {mc['prot_ft_noip_reliability']:.3f}"},
    {"Check": f"Within-exact-4-digit-allele ERAP1 length ({mc['within_exact_allele_n_alleles']} alleles, N={mc['within_exact_allele_n_obs']})", "Estimate": round(mc["within_exact_allele_erap1_len_r"], 4), "Detail": f"Exact 10! whole-patient permutation P = {s8_mon['exact_two_sided_patient_permutation_p']:.5f} (3,628,800 perms)"},
    {"Check": "APPM-breadth partial r | Tumor Purity", "Estimate": round(mc["appm_breadth_partial_r_purity"], 4), "Detail": f"p = {mc['appm_breadth_partial_p_purity']:.4f}; ImmuneScore partial r = {mc['appm_breadth_partial_r_immune']:.4f} (p={mc['appm_breadth_partial_p_immune']:.4f})"},
])

  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("HLA-I yield" = BLUE, "HLA-II yield" = PURPLE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Standardized beta (95% HC3 CI)", color = NULL, title = "Across-gene PTM & topology routing (N=7,594)")

pM2 <- ggplot(py$m2_pt, aes(x = appm_core_prot_noIP, y = log2_n_hlai_peptides)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = TEAL, fill = LBLUE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, color = NAVY) +
  geom_text(aes(label = gsub("^C3L-|^C3N-", "", sample_id)), vjust = -0.7, size = 2.8) +
  labs(x = "Independent noIP tumor APPM core protein", y = "log2(HLA-I peptide breadth)", title = "Tumor APPM core vs. HLA-I breadth (N=10)")

pM3 <- ggplot(py$m_al, aes(x = erap1_within_allele, y = len_within_allele)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = ORANGE, fill = GOLD, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = BLUE, alpha = 0.85) +
  labs(x = "Within-allele demeaned ERAP1 protein (noIP)", y = "Within-allele demeaned peptide length (aa)", title = "Within-4-digit-allele ERAP1 trimming (16 alleles)")

pM4 <- py$m_jk |>
  pivot_longer(c(r_appm_breadth_noIP, r_erap1_len_noIP), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(Metric = recode(Metric, r_appm_breadth_noIP = "APPM vs. breadth (noIP)", r_erap1_len_noIP = "ERAP1 vs. length (noIP)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = omitted_patient, y = r, color = Metric, group = Metric)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("APPM vs. breadth (noIP)" = TEAL, "ERAP1 vs. length (noIP)" = BLUE)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Omitted LUAD patient", y = "Leave-one-tumor-out Pearson r", color = NULL, title = "10-tumor jackknife stability")

tagged((pM1 + pM2) / (pM3 + pM4))
```

**What do we see?**

Tables 3.6–3.10 and Figure 3.3 connect surface HLA-I flux directly to ubiquitin-proteasome turnover and ERAP1 trimming in primary LUAD tumors (`N = 10`):

- **Compartment-specific six-omic routing across `N = 7,594` proteins (Tables 3.6–3.7):** `HLA-I` peptide breadth tracks molecular weight (`+0.4704`), spectral protein abundance (`+0.3512`), and **`K-epsilon-GG` ubiquitylation (`std_beta = +0.1993`, `t = 18.72`)**, with zero secretory/ER enrichment (`-0.0068`, `p = 0.475`) or lysine-acetylation coupling (`-0.0060`, `p = 0.596`). By contrast, `HLA-II` breadth enriches sharply for secretory/ER/membrane topology (`+0.2532`, `t = 23.00`) and lysine acetylation (`+0.1604`), so the paired `(HLA-I - HLA-II)` differential yields positive `K-epsilon-GG` routing (`+0.0444`, `p = 0.0014` after explicit lysine-count adjustment, where `K-epsilon-GG -> HLA-I` stays `+0.1994`, `p = 1.29e-76`) and negative secretory/acetyl contrast (`-0.2022` and `-0.1345`).
- **Within-gene across-patient ubiquitin flux (Tables 3.8 & 3.10):** Conditioning on both gene and patient fixed effects in independent `noIP` aliquots (`N = 10,056` pairs, `1,816` genes) yields positive `HLA-I` ubiquitylation coupling (`beta_ub = +0.0464`, `gene-clustered p = 0.0122`, `8/10` tumors positive, `signflip p = 0.0312`), replicated in `FT` (`+0.0416`, `p = 0.0130`), preserved under Gauss-Seidel two-way demeaning with CGM two-way SEs (`+0.0565`, `SE = 0.0168`), and confirmed by `2SLS` IV (`Ub IV beta = +0.0457` when `FT` instruments `noIP`; residual reliability $r = 0.824$). Even for identical `HLA-I` peptides (`356` sequences, `1,609` obs), parent proteome and `K-epsilon-GG` explain only `0.71%` (`R^2 = 0.0071`) of intensity variation.
- **Tumor `APPM` breadth and within-allele `ERAP1` trimming (Tables 3.9–3.10):** Patient-level `APPM` core protein abundance predicts $\log_2$ `HLA-I` breadth across all `10` tumors ($r = +0.7615$, `perm p = 0.0104` in `FT`; $r = +0.7288$ in `noIP`), holding after conditioning on tumor purity (`partial r = +0.7260`, `p = 0.0268`) or `ESTIMATE` ImmuneScore ($r = +0.7237$, `p = 0.0275`). Meanwhile, endogenous `ERAP1` protein inversely predicts peptide length (`noIP r = -0.6783`, `p = 0.0283`) and holds strongly **within exact 4-digit alleles** across `16` shared alleles (`N = 35` allele-patient cells, $r = -0.7452$, `OLS p = 2.83e-07`, patient-clustered `p = 2.22e-04`), staying negative across every 10-tumor jackknife drop.

**Decision point:**

Paired compositional shifts generalize across lineages (`LOLO 0.948`) and zero shared HLA alleles (`SK-Mel-28 1.000`) through `HLA-A/B/C` locus shifts (`0.889`), while tumor `K-epsilon-GG` and `ERAP1` link surface peptides to intracellular routing. I next move to [Report 04](04_censoring_gatekeepers_and_sensitivity.html) to examine left-censored detection attrition, linear molar stoichiometry, `HAP1` `Sec61` gatekeepers, and ablation/depth curves.
